basics.name: Gaurav Joshi
basics.label: Computer Vision, Agentic AI, Computer-Use Agents, Deep Learning
basics.summary: My research sits at the intersection of computer vision and agentic AI, focusing on how models perceive, reason about, and act within visual and digital environments. This includes work on inverse graphics, procedural content generation, and computer-use agents that translate visual and expert knowledge into executable actions.

work.name: UC San Diego – Center for Visual Computing
work.summary: Advisors: Manmohan Chandraker (Prof., UCSD), Kunal Gupta (PhD, UCSD)
highlights: BlendCUA: Self-Evolving Computer-Use Harness for Blender (first author). Built a computer-use agent that turns natural-language briefs and reference images into Blender assets across modelling, materials, physics simulation and animation, and that improves its own harness (tools, skills, plan checks) from experience with the model kept frozen.

Proposed learning from the defects in the agent's finished work instead of from successful trajectories, and implemented the loop end to end: an independent checker agent, a curator agent that attributes each defect to the plan, review, execution or reference views, and a rebuild gate that keeps a new skill or tool only if it fixes the defect.
Outperformed existing harnesses such as Claude Code and Codex on held-out tasks, with most learned tools and skills reused on later tasks. Under review at ICLR 2027.

Procedural Material Generation from Expert Workflows (ECCV 2026). Researched agentic LLM systems that learn from expert video demonstrations and reason over expert workflows to produce executable outputs, applied to procedural materials in Blender.
Knowledge extraction: built automated pipelines that turn Blender tutorial videos into structured procedural knowledge using video understanding and LLM-based reasoning.
Generation: helped develop retrieval-time reasoning agents that use this knowledge to plan expert-style material creation processes and compile them into executable Blender node graphs.
Supported expert and large-scale user studies showing improved workflow quality over graph-only generation baselines; paper accepted at ECCV 2026.

work.name: FluenTalk
work.summary: Voice-based AI assistant for improving spoken English
highlights: Built a voice-based AI assistant web app for improving spoken English, tested with 200+ students.
Developed a production web app integrating OpenAI APIs for real-time voice interaction, grammar correction, and fluency feedback across practice modes such as debates and passage reading.
Architected the full-stack system: Django backend, React frontend, Firebase authentication, CockroachDB database.
Designed ML-driven feedback mechanisms improving user engagement and measurable learning outcomes.

work.name: IIT Gandhinagar – CVIG Lab
work.summary: Advisors: Shanmuganathan Raman (Prof., IITGn), Ashish Tiwari (PhD, IITGn)
highlights: Worked on inverse modeling for outdoor scenes from single images.
Used Gaussian Splatting and NeRF models to represent outdoor scenes and perform reconstruction/re-rendering.

work.name: Purdue University – IDEAS Lab
work.summary: Advisors: Aniket Bera (Associate Prof., Purdue), Hrishikesh Vishwanath (PhD, Purdue)
highlights: Worked on operator learning (neural operators) to build surrogates for fluid simulation (Navier-Stokes equations).
Worked on human-pair motion generation using generative neural operators.

work.name: Google Summer of Code — OpenAstronomy / Stingray
work.summary: Advisors: Daniela Huppenkothen (Univ. of Amsterdam), Matteo Bachetti (INAF, Italy)
highlights: Developed a Gaussian Processes inference tool to calculate the evidence of a QPO (Quasi-Periodic Oscillation) signal in astronomical time series from events like GRBs and magnetar/solar flares.
Made demonstration and tutorial notebooks on Bayesian inference and the project tool.
Used Jax, TinyGP, JaxNS, and tensorflow_probability.
Open-source project funded under the Google Summer of Code program.

projects.name: PDEs Solving using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
highlights: Implemented PINNs to solve Laplace equations for various Dirichlet conditions.
Comparative evaluation against analytic and mesh methods.
Tools: TensorFlow, LaTeX.

projects.name: Computational Statistics eBook
highlights: Wrote an online book on computational statistics covering the math behind Bayesian data analysis and parameter estimation.
Covered random variable generation, Monte Carlo integration, MCMC (MH, HMC, Gibbs), Gaussian processes, information theory, sequential Monte Carlo, and graphical models.

projects.name: Effective Sensor Placement using Neural Processes
highlights: Built an ML pipeline using conditional neural processes for effective pollution sensor placement.
Used CAMx-simulated pollution data to predict future pollution levels and place sensors via a mutual information criterion.
Compared fit quality across neural processes, Gaussian processes, and other models.
Tools: PyTorch, Jax, DeepSensor.
